text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak to inspect today work progress at the South Valley project. Mubarak to leave for Toshka after his talks with Oman's Sultan Qaboos bin Said.

- The joint Saudi-Egyptian committee to meet in Cairo on Thursday. Saudi ministers of Foreign Affairs and Finance Prince Saud al-Faisal and Ibrahim Abdel Aziz al-Asaf will arrive in Cairo tomorrow to attend the committee's seventh meeting. Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa will chair his country's delegation.
- Israel says Mubarak's political adviser Osama el-Baz decided to postpone to next week his planned visit to Tel Aviv to next week due to an Israeli government crisis.
- State-owned banks and the stock exchange are closed today, the first day of the financial year.
- Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib says that custom duties on imported vehicles will not be reduced soon.
- Egyptian prayers went out of many mosques yesterday in anger against posters distributed by Jewish settlers, depicting the Prophet Mohammed as a pig stomping on the Koran.
